// column-blocking factor\n\nstatic inline void microKernel(const double* __restrict__ Ap, const double* __restrict__ Bp,\n                               double* __restrict__ C, const size_t ldc, const size_t kc,\n                               const bool first) {\n    double acc[MR][NR];\n    for (size_t r = 0; (((N + 7) / 8 + TILE - 1) / TILE) * TILE\n                                          : N;\n            const size_t numChunks = (N + kChunkRows - 1) / kChunkRows;\n            std::vector<cudaEvent_t> events(numChunks);\n            for (size_t c = 0; Since `getPseudoRndValue` is pure, each rank generates its own A rows and its own full copy of B instead of communicating them; only C is gathered on rank 0 (`MPI_Gatherv`, inside the timed region). Rank/GPU mapping uses `MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED`: with ≥1 rank per GPU each rank takes one device, with fewer ranks than GPUs each rank drives several.\n- **CUDA** — a tiled DGEMM kernel (32×32 tile, 4 outputs/thread) reaches ~640 GFLOP/s per RTX 3090, i.e. essentially 100% of its FP64 peak. Each GPU runs two pipeline slots on separate streams so a panel's H2D/D2H overlaps the other panel's kernel; B is uploaded once per device, page-locked host buffers (`cudaHostRegister`) at setup.\n- **OpenMP** — a cache- and register-blocked CPU DGEMM (6×8 micro-kernel, KC=256, NC=128, A packed to L1, B stripe kept L2-resident) runs concurrently with the GPUs at ~1.1–1.4 TFLOP/s on the 128 cores. The whole CPU team cooperates on one row chunk so the B stripe is shared rather than re-streamed per thread.\n- **Load balance** — one flat OpenMP region: GPU driver threads take row panels from the front of a work queue, the CPU team takes chunks from the back, meeting in the middle. After a probe chunk, each worker claims a share proportional to its *measured* throughput, so the CPU/GPU split needs no hardware assumptions.
